messages.subject: dbWriteTable fails after a truncate in a transaction
messages.subject_clean: dbWriteTable fails after a truncate in a transaction
messages.body_plain:
Hi, 

I'm trying to truncate a table and then to copy new records into this 
table, in a same transaction :

test <- data.frame(test=c("test0", "test1"))
dbGetQuery(con, "BEGIN TRANSACTION")    
rs <- dbSendQuery(con,  "TRUNCATE test")
dbWriteTable(con, "test", test, append = T, row.names = F)
dbCommit(con)

The dbWriteTable function fails and the process gets stucked. 
Nevertheless it works if I don't truncate the table before, and it also 
works if I replace the dbWriteTable function with sets of INSERT INTO 
statements ...

Any idea of how to fix it ?

Thanks, 

Juliette

messages.subject: Re: [R-sig-DB] R and PostgreSQL - Writing data?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

PostgreSQL have library function PQexecParams and also supports prepared statements.
String expansion in the SQL statement is cumbersome for escaping special characters and
therefore error prone.

I just commited to the SVN repository a very simple and primitive implementation that
allows to pass vector of characters as parameters.

A sample statement is like:

    res <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM rockdata WHERE peri > $1 AND shape < $2 LIMIT $3", c(4000, 0.2, 10))
    print(res)

The syntax for a positional parameter is a dollar sign ($) followed by digits
rather than a colon followed by digits in PostgreSQL.
http://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.2/static/sql-syntax-lexical.html#SQL-SYNTAX-SPECIAL-CHARS

This mechanism is required for the support of prepared statements.
It is nicer if I could make automatic conversions for various type and binary transfer, 
but this is not implemented right now.
So all parameters are simply passed as strings at the moment.

Note this is the very initial implementation and the interface may change.

Any enhancement, feedback, or test case/program is welcome.
Especially, on what would be the best interface/syntax.

Best regards,
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

Advanced Science Research Center,
Kanazawa University,
13-1 Takara-machi, 
Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan

messages.subject: Re: Connecting to Herokupostgres Standalone database with RPostgreSQL
messages.subject_clean: Connecting to Herokupostgres Standalone database with RPostgreSQL
messages.body_plain:
There looks to be some difficulty connect through SSL using RPostgreSQL. 
 There is a discussiong 
here: https://groups.google.com/d/topic/rpostgresql-dev/ELnVUJqjDbk/discussion

If you haven't yet figured out how to connect to Heroku's stand alone DB 
through R, you can do it using the JDBC connection.  A good description is 
here: 
 http://ryepup.unwashedmeme.com/blog/2010/11/17/working-with-r-postgresql-ssl-and-mssql/

Assuming that the jar file is in your local directory, the code to connect 
will look like this:

library('RJDBC')
pgsql <- JDBC("org.postgresql.Driver", "./postgresql-9.2-1002.jdbc4.jar", 
"`")
testdb <- dbConnect(pgsql, 
"jdbc:postgresql://host:port/dbname?user=user&password=password&ssl=true&sslfactory=org.postgresql.ssl.NonValidatingFactory")

Hope this helps RPostgreSQL can be updated to support the sslmode option.

messages.subject: Re: RPostgreSQL port number
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,

Why don't you just duplicate using the active connection?
con <- dbConnect('PostgreSQL', blah, blahh,...)
con2 <- dbConnect(con)

I will add the port number in next release.

However, note that dbGetInfo do not return the password
and I don't think we make it return the password.  
--
